speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Since I am reviewing a newborn with respiratory distress, I will ask my questions directly as if examining this infant. What is your baby's gestational age at birth, and was there any difficulty during delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given the premature onset of labor and the early presentation of distress, have you noticed any grunting, nasal flaring, or recession at the base of the ribs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hyaline Membrane Disease (Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome).
The clinical picture of prematurity (33 weeks) combined with immediate respiratory distress, grunting, and significant retractions is classic for RDS. I am not requesting further tests as the diagnosis is clinically evident and urgent management with CPAP is required.
